baseline.measurement: The reviewed rich Desk producer tree with the sandbox job service, deferred request completion, the bridge between interoperability values and the sandbox value codec, the library that builds verified sandbox plans from source, the shared sandbox capability that Desk hosts, the sandbox identity digests, the canonical sandbox profile descriptor, the canonical sandbox artifact format, canonical schema bytes with the JSON schema reader, canonical sandbox module declarations, closed sandbox schemas, the live table of installed sandbox modules, the durable sandbox module store, the shared sandbox capability's module operations and intents, Desk's screens for the shared sandbox, and the sandbox job service lending jobs to worker cores, library interval timers on uptime with the RPC rate limiter no longer requiring datetime.f, the ISO weekday and wall-clock validity words, and the POSIX TZ zone library, Daybook schedule recurrence, the Daybook automation store and its owner, the reminder runner and service, which Desk hosts, Daybook's reminders view with its create steps, and the growing record tables the Daybook store shares, and the scheduled-action catalog with its portable dispatch contract, and the Daybook store and owner speaking the catalog and dispatch contract, and the durable schedule permissions Desk's broker will match runs against, and Desk lending the Agent's services and Daybook's automations only to their own components, and Daybook handing Agent runs to the broker through the dispatch client, and Desk's schedule broker, which checks each scheduled run against the permissions and compiles its authority from them, and Agent turns that run on a model they name, with each provider reporting its room for a turn's input, and the blob slots records use to hold bytes of any length, shared by the stores, and the Agent's run store, which records each scheduled run once, before its provider starts, with how it ended and its transcript, and the Agent's dispatcher, which runs the scheduled work Desk's broker hands it in a conversation of its own, on the model it names, one run at a time with chat waiting behind, and the Agent's view of its scheduled runs, which lists them newest first and opens a kept run's transcript, and the Desk adapter that makes the Agent's dispatcher the schedule broker's handler, through the Agent's public service seam, and Desk hosting the Agent's dispatcher and the schedule broker, lending the dispatcher to the Agent and the broker's client to Daybook, and Desk's screens for scheduled runs: the approval of a schedule and the run permissions, with Desk's sandbox screens and these sharing one screen slot, and Desk asking before it closes while a scheduled run is in flight or waiting, and Daybook's reminders view renamed its automations view, which will show Agent runs too, and Daybook's automations view making Agent runs from the model list Desk's broker gives, which it reads itself, and Daybook's pages for making an Agent run, whose prompt editor copies, cuts and pastes through the clipboard, and a schedule's details in Daybook, which say an Agent run's model and limits in the catalog's words that Desk's approval now uses too, and a value system and resource contract that carry a document of up to 16 MiB, with Library's snapshot reading into a buffer of exactly the document's size, and a directory of resource owners that Desk keeps and Library publishes its documents' owner in, one-use grants for an Agent run's requests shared by the tool gateway, and a scheduled run reading its one exact document as itself while it starts, and OpenAI turns whose input, request body and tool history are sized to what they hold, with the body lent to the HTTP request, and the media layer below the widgets (sources, file kinds, pictures and documents), the Markdown reader with the HTML entity list, the picture, media and document widgets, the shared rule for the path a document's link names, the native document family with its DOC1 packer, the document view's capture with the producer's document lowering, the document view's figures described to the rich side as clipped pictures, Adler-32 beside the CRCs, the resumable inflater, the resumable PNG decoder, PNG picture copies, gzip bodies inflated by the buffered HTTP exchange, MD5 and RC4 for PDF's security handler, the PDF lexer and stream filters, the PDF file layer, the PDF CMap reader with the text tables, the PDF page tree, the PDF fonts with the content interpreter, the PDF page layout with its tagged structure, the PDF standard security handler, the PDF destinations, links and outline with number and name trees and text strings, and the PDF pictures as files with the QOI encoder by rows, placed on their pages as figures, and object streams indexed once, and documents read in parts as a view reaches them, with PDFs read as documents a page at a time, which File Explorer's preview shows, and pictures a document holds made into files in steps for its view, and a PDF page's links placed over the text they cover, and a document's contents, a PDF's outline or pages, shown as a tree in place of the document, each entry open or closed as the document says and its title drawn and published as untrusted text, and a PDF's page labels from every pair of its number tree, and document views' work counted beside pictures' for hosts' service passes, and a PDF destination's place on its page found among the blocks where they lie, and a document's contents published to a rich terminal as the item view their tree gives, and a PDF file holding each object stream it decodes, and a PDF page's columns found by their gutters, and AES's CBC mode beside GCM, both under one guard with one status vocabulary, and PDFs encrypted with AES-128 and AES-256 opened by the standard security handler, with SHA-384 beside SHA-512, and prompts and Desk's Ask prompt published as TEXT fields through the field model, and dialogs that ask without blocking, captured as canonical dialog models with their content codec and the UIDL dialog snapshot and lowered by the hybrid producer through the DLG1 codec, with Daybook, Library and Streams asking their questions through the shared dialog, and the UIDL dialog element, a framed container whose title and leading labels are its message, which the dialog snapshot captures with its contents and the producer lowers as a dialog around them, with Desk's screens framed as such dialogs, and the shell candidate letting an overlay pane lie over the panes beneath it, its document in a modal region over the whole screen

filesystem.note: Scale and architecture qualification use the generic VFS contract; ext4 is an optional integration backend.

public_applet_seams.purpose: Desk-owned capability selection policy uses Agent's public access-profile selector contract.
Desk-owned access policy composes the public Agent service without importing Agent internals.
Desk product composition borrows Daybook's public resource-owner service.
Desk product composition hosts Daybook's public reminder service: it opens it over the Practice filesystem, ticks it, lends it, and shows its notices.
Desk's schedule broker compiles each scheduled run's frozen authority with the Agent's public Mandate-run constructor, through the one public Agent composition seam, as Desk's chat factory does.

Desk's schedule broker gets the Agent's scheduled-run dispatcher as its handler, through the one public Agent composition seam: the dispatcher's own words start, follow and cancel runs, list the models and vet approvals.

composition_roots.purpose: Optional rich-terminal Desk boot composition: binds the unchanged Desk applet to the generic APT-1 engine and UIDL adapter so no applet imports the rich terminal. Loaded only by the desktop-apt1 autoexec; no module may import it.

query_workloads.required_behavior: bounded index-page reads independent of corpus cardinality
index seek followed by bounded candidate verification

library_model_workload.per_record_cardinality: variable tags, lineage facts, and revisions without fixed inline aggregate ceilings
library_model_workload.content_shape: variable-size and chunked content, including documents beyond whole-buffer limits

streams_model_workload.source_distribution: skewed observation and retained-attempt histories across enabled and disabled sources
streams_model_workload.query_shape: deep time, source, thread, and text-candidate continuation

sr1_contract.capacity_role: SR1 prototype cell bounds, not supported product limits

sr2.payload: named payload profiles with body and connection storage separate from each cell
sr2.http: caller-owned strict request framing, copied routing, bounded response sources and exact interleaved cooperative request-to-response journeys under pool pressure
qualification: one body larger than 4096 bytes without enlarging every cell
measured live workspace memory and deterministic owner-step cost
sr2.cutover_rule: the unreleased SR1 layout is replaced atomically; no parallel layout, ABI selector, adapter, migration, deprecation path, or old-layout reader; general code does not persist raw descriptors

sr3.runtime_relation: durable queues and spools are separate from the active-cell pool
sr3.capacity: independent item and byte bounds with exact-full and one-over behavior
sr3.acceptance: exact payload snapshot and attempt identity commit before durable acceptance
sr3.delivery: durable ready, active, terminal, receipt, stale-revision, cancellation, cleanup-failure, and visible indeterminate truth with current-only recovery
sr3.recovery: self-identifying current format, interrupted publication, corrupt or unknown refusal, restart, receipts, and visible indeterminate work; prerelease changes replace the prototype
sr3.composition: caller-owned dispatch binds exact durable authority to a fitting SR2 cell, commits active authority before runtime effect, and retires the cell only after durable terminal evidence
sr3.retirement: revision-checked logical cleanup and current-only bounded two-bank live-set compaction remove unreachable records and payloads, reopen the selected bank, and physically remove the old bank
sr3.retry: no automatic indeterminate-effect retry without a safe declared idempotency contract
qualification: current configuration and operational record codecs
delivery, receipt, stale-revision, indeterminate-recovery, and logical-cleanup journeys
SR2 dispatch composition with authority-before-effect and finite runtime retirement
bounded live-set compaction, old-bank removal, selected-bank reopen, and cold physical audit
sr3.cutover_rule: the unreleased durable prototype has one current record and compaction path; no parallel format, version selector, adapter, migration, deprecation path, or old-layout reader remains

sr6.purpose: qualify supported workload profiles without redesigning runtime semantics or durable record shapes

future_sr6.workload: derive production-supported profiles from the qualified SR2 runtime and SR3 deterministic durable path
must_not_require: reuse of historical source and observation cardinalities

hot_path_budgets.cold_open_working_memory: two caller-owned bytes per largest valid-slot page plus fixed audit work

hot_path_budgets.staging_publication_reservation: one application-root page within the 128-page physical transaction arena

live_topology.staging_publication_reservation: one application-root page within the 128-page physical transaction arena

hot_path_budget_amendment.resolved: L12 admits each staged mutation only when its dynamic tree-height reservation and the next application-root page fit the bounded physical staging arena; physical publications split long logical operations without advancing their logical generation, and two-bank compaction replaces the prior bank arena with an explicitly owned target-build arena.
evidence: all-tree page-read, page-write, and comparison telemetry
2h+1 mutation-page reservation from the tallest current staging root
two-byte-per-page cold ownership and structural-uniqueness audit
physical and final publication paths with distinct logical-generation semantics

existing_guest_counters: PBLOB chunk and manifest reads and writes
PBLOB transferred bytes and peak working memory
Library reclaim steps and moved pages
hot_path_baseline.clarification: Library B+tree counters report logical 4,096-byte checked-page activity across all fifteen live trees. PERF-EXTMEM remains external-memory traffic, not an allocation counter or a substitute for logical page telemetry.

coverage.missing: SR6 production workload-derived concurrency, throughput, latency, memory, disk-amplification, and recovery evidence
isolated launch, close, relayout, dispatch, and repaint telemetry

representative_bounds.shape: 32 results from the large-host body-postings tree
dynamic tallest-root mutation reservation plus one application-root page
representative_bounds.admission: checked against current usage of the bounded 128-page physical staging arena before each mutation

complexity_ledger.operation: staged document, collection, and posting mutation publication
complexity_ledger.current_structure: fifteen copy-on-write indexes with each staged mutation admitted against a bounded high-water physical arena
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O((changed keys + candidate postings) log n)
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: long logical operations may require multiple bounded physical publications whose count follows live tree height and changed-key volume
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: delivered in L12: reserve the tallest mutation path and next application-root page inside the current physical arena, publishing a physical checkpoint when the next mutation would not fit

complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(sources + observations + keys) bytes per load/save
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: every mutation rewrites and verifies aggregate state
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: retain only as frozen compatibility evidence until SR6 retirement; derive any future operational persistence from the SR2 flow and delivery semantics in SR3, never from the superseded observation corpus

complexity_ledger.scale_risk: append/load cost and memory grow with the complete retained conversation
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: paged records, ranged content, and indexed conversation access

complexity_ledger.current_structure: one whole text document plus fixed entry array
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(document bytes + entry count) per reload
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: the full journal is reparsed and materialized
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: chunked text or indexed entry records with date/tag indexes

complexity_ledger.current_structure: one checksummed file holding every schedule, firing and create key, replaced whole
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(schedules + occurrences + keys) bytes and checks per commit and per load
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: every reminder change and every firing rewrites, verifies and rechecks the whole store
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: paged schedule and occurrence records on persistence/ once reminder counts make whole-file commits slow

complexity_ledger.operation: open, find, load, and search documents
complexity_ledger.current_structure: fixed array of complete document buffers
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: large documents and many tabs consume fixed whole-buffer slots
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: per-document piece/gap state, ranged VFS I/O, and incremental search

complexity_ledger.current_structure: one allocated block of copied row records, sized to the directory, with pairwise swap sort
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(directory entries squared) sort after O(entries) materialization
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: paged directory source with stable IDs and scalable ordering

complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(file bytes + fixed matrix cells) parse/materialization
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: sparse or large sheets pay dense storage and hard row/column ceilings
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: sparse tiled cells and dependency-indexed incremental recalculation

complexity_ledger.current_structure: fixed catalogs and linear visible-order traversal
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(apps + services + visible slots) host operations
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: launch, lookup, and layout work grow through repeated linear scans
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: indexed host slots plus explicit visible order and incremental layout

complexity_ledger.scale_risk: lookup latency and hard capacity grow with the complete registry
resource resolution scans the complete live registry

complexity_ledger.current_structure: fixed pointer ring plus globally guarded dispatch scratch
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: bounded O(1) queueing but fixed aggregate capacity and shared serialization
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: independent buses contend through process-global guards and cannot express caller-selected backpressure
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: per-instance queues/guards with explicit capacity and bounded scheduling

complexity_ledger.operation: resource acquisition, retained dispatch, and release
complexity_ledger.current_structure: caller-sized slot/lease arrays with direct member-to-slot dispatch metadata and a shared cold-control-plane scratch trampoline
complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(slots + leases) lifecycle lookup with cross-pool lifecycle serialization, and O(1) per-pool guarded handler entry/exit
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: very large simultaneous owner sets still scan caller storage and high-rate acquisition/release across independent pools still contends, though request dispatch is independent of registry and pool cardinality
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: add caller-supplied slot/lease indexes and per-pool lifecycle workspaces only when measured concurrent-owner or lifecycle throughput exceeds the bounded design

complexity_ledger.current_complexity: O(document bytes) parse and O(elements) ID lookup
complexity_ledger.scale_risk: large UI documents hit aggregate limits and repeated linear lookup
complexity_ledger.replacement_requirement: per-instance arenas with indexed IDs and bounded render caches
